newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends down on weak sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends down on weak sentiment.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended down on Friday on weak market sentiment despite overnight gains on the London Metal Exchange, traders said.
The most active January 1997 contract ended at 20,210 yuan ($2,434) per tonne, losing 140 yuan. It opened at an intra-day high of 20,400 and hit a low of 20,110.
October fell 120 to 20,580 yuan, November 160 to 20,320, December 120 to 20,230, February and March 150 to 20,200, April 120 to 20,280.
Combined volume fell to 26,030 tonnes from 32,180.
Copper opened up but fell steadily for most of the session due to profit-taking and fresh selling.
Traders said that copper on the LME was still below the key $1,970 resistance level despite rises over the past few days, which triggered disappointment selling in Shanghai.
"Profit-taking and hedge-selling emerged at high levels because many investors believed that gains on the LME lacked fundamental support," one trader said.
"Institutions did not dare to push copper sharply up given the weak domestic spot demand," he added.
Analysts expect copper to continue to move in a narrow range of 20,000 and 20,500 in the next few days.
Aluminium ended down. The only traded October contract closed at 13,950 yuan, losing 50 yuan.
Combined volume fell to 300 tonnes from 370.
